title: Systems Empowerment: Onboarding, Role Concordance, and Internal Tooling Map
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose
This playbook documents the canonical onboarding and role-access model for Redwood contributors, the mapping between role levels and tool privileges, and the operational SLAs for provisioning. It is intended to reduce friction during hire/onboard/role-change events and to make responsibilities and escalation paths explicit.

Scope
- Audience: new hires, hiring managers, people-ops partners, IT, security, and team leads.
- Tools covered: Okta SSO, GitHub org, Google Cloud projects, Redwood Console (internal), Rampboard (onboarding tracker), Slack, Jira, Confluence, LastPass/KMS, and internal build/deploy pipelines.

Owner and Contacts
- Playbook owner: People Ops (Asha Patel)
- Escalation: IT & Security Triage (it-triage@redwood.com) for access failures beyond SLA
- Provisioning queue: rampboard@redwood.com (monitored M-F 08:00–18:00 PT)

Goals
1. New hire self-sufficiency within 7 business days for customer-facing engineers and within 5 business days for non-customer-facing roles.
2. Deterministic access mapping that minimizes over-provisioning.
3. Clear role-change process that preserves auditability and reduces interruptions to product work.

High-level Onboarding Flow (summary)
1. Offer accepted -> People Ops triggers a Rampboard entry (includes start date, role, manager, equipment).
2. Pre-boarding (3–10 days before start): Okta invite, company handbook access, mandatory training assignments.
3. Day 0: Badge activation, laptop checkout (if required), Slack workspace welcome, GitHub invite.
4. Day 1–7: Role-specific access granted in waves (see Provisioning SLA). Manager runs 30/60/90 cadence using the manager checklist in this doc.

Provisioning SLA (operational commitments)
- Okta SSO account: within 24 hours of Rampboard entry.
- GitHub least-privilege org membership: within 24 hours for core org repos; repo-specific access within 48 hours.
- Google Cloud project viewer access: within 48 hours; Editor-level or service account access requires manager approval and security review (72 hours).
- Redwood Console (internal): Console-level read access within 24 hours; deploy permissions and model-serving keys require a dedicated approval workflow (up to 5 business days).
- Jira and Confluence: defaults on Day 0; project-level role grants within 48 hours.

Role Concordance and Tool Matrix (how roles map to tool privileges)
Note: this matrix favors least-privilege by default. For brevity we show primary role categories. To request exceptions, use the Access Exception Request form (internal link).

| Role Category | Okta Group | GitHub Org/Teams | GCP Projects | Redwood Console | Jira Projects | Notes |
|---------------|-----------:|-----------------:|-------------:|----------------:|--------------:|------|
| IC-1 (new engineer) | engineers-ic | org:read-only, team:team-{product}:write after probation | viewer | console-read | project-contributor | Elevated write after manager approval and 30-day review |
| IC-2/IC-3 | engineers-core | org:repo-contributor, team access per product | viewer/editor (limited) | console-deploy-read | project-admin (limited) | Service account work requires security checklist |
| IC-4/IC-5 (senior) | engineers-senior | repo-admin for owned services | editor / SA with limited keys | console-deploy | project-admin | Ownership includes creating new infra repos and service accounts |
| Manager-1/Manager-2 | managers | managers-team-* (Org membership + team admin) | project-owner (select) | console-admin (team-scoped) | project-admin | Manager approval required on all elevated access requests |
| Product & Design | product, design | org:repo-contributor | viewer | console-read | project-contributor | Product PMs get access to feature flags and telemetry views |
| Eng-SRE & Infra | infra-ops | org:repo-admin, infra-team | project-owner, billing-view | console-admin | project-admin | SREs get broad role to operate infra; privileged actions logged to audit pipelines |

(If you need a CSV export of this matrix, request it from people-ops.)

Detailed Onboarding Tasks (first 30 days)
- Before Day 0
  1. People Ops creates Rampboard and attaches job description, manager details, start date.
  2. IT provisions a temporary Okta invite and schedules equipment delivery.
  3. Security assigns required trainings to the new user in the learning platform.

- Day 0
  1. Activate Okta, join Slack, read the Employee Handbook.
  2. Complete mandatory compliance and security training modules (expected 2–3 hours).
  3. Confirm laptop and network access; file IT ticket if hardware missing.

- Day 1–7
  1. Receive GitHub invite and accept organization invite.
  2. Get Confluence and Jira baseline access.
  3. Meet the buddy and immediate team; run through the product walkthrough.
  4. Complete 30-day kickoff meeting with manager (agenda template in Confluence).

- Day 8–30
  1. Apply for additional access as required by job tasks (use the internal Access Request Jira template).
  2. First code review and merge permissions established.
  3. Complete initial onboarding projects and checkpoint with manager.

Role Change and Access Transition Process
1. Manager files a Role-Change petition in Rampboard and selects new level and effective date.
2. People Ops reviews and confirms compensation/admin changes.
3. IT and Security run an automated policy comparison to compute delta of privileges.
4. Approvals: Manager + Security (for any infra/elevated / SA changes).
5. Execution: staged access modifications are applied on the effective date, and old privileges are retained for a 7-day overlap window for rollback.
6. Audit: change automatically logged and emailed to manager + people-ops.

Least-Privilege Exceptions and Temporary Access
- Temporary elevated access is granted via short-lived service sessions or time-bound Okta groups, not by permanent membership where possible.
- Standard exception duration: 72 hours, extendable once with manager approval. All exceptions must be requested through the Access Exception Request form and include justification, scope, and rollback plan.

Manager Checklists (short)
- Day 1 Manager Checklist:
  - Introduce buddy and 1:1 schedule
  - Confirm Rampboard details and equipment
  - Review first-week goals and learning resources
  - Verify baseline access (Okta, Slack, GitHub, Confluence, Jira)
- 30/60/90 Template (link):
  - 30d: basic contributor impact, access sufficiency, blockers
  - 60d: technical ownership, cross-team dependencies, performance inputs
  - 90d: promotion readiness discussion (if applicable) and role alignment

Operational Runbook Snippets (when access fails)
1. Confirm Rampboard entry is complete and correct.
2. Check Okta event logs for invite acceptance (okta-admin console).
3. Open a ticket to IT with subject: [Access Failure] {new-hire-name} {tool} and include Rampboard URL.
4. If SLA breached >48 hours for core access, escalate to it-triage@redwood.com with ticket ID and manager confirmation.

Audit and Reporting
- People Ops publishes a weekly onboarding report (CSV) with statuses: invited, activated, baseline access, role-specific access pending, escalations.
- Security runs quarterly access reviews where group memberships are compared against the expected Role Concordance Matrix. Findings are reported to the Leadership Security Review.

Tool-specific Notes and Examples
- Okta: Primary groups follow the naming convention {org}-{role}-{level}, e.g., redwood-engineer-ic3. Admins must include justification on membership changes.
- GitHub: New repos default to 'org:private' with branch protection templates applied. To request repo-admin: complete the repo-ownership form and include a codeowners file.
- GCP: Provisioning requires a billing owner tag and security tagging; service account keys are disabled by default and require a separate request to infra-security.
- Redwood Console (internal): Access modeled as Console Role -> Team -> Environment. Example roles: console-read, console-deploy, console-admin. Audit logs for deploy events are forwarded to the telemetry pipeline.

Improving the Playbook
- Submit tool or process gaps to the People Ops backlog via the 'Onboarding & Tools' Jira project.
- Quarterly review cycle: People Ops + IT + Security + two engineering reps.

Appendix: Quick CLI & Requests
- Rampboard create (manager): curl -X POST https://internal-api/rampboard/create -d '{"name":"New Hire", "start":"2026-03-01", "role":"IC-2", "manager":"manager@redwood.com"}'
- Access request template (Jira): Project ONB, Issue type: Access Request; fields: user, requested-groups, justification, expiration-date.

Glossary
- Rampboard: internal onboarding tracker and ticketing queue.
- Least-Privilege: default policy to grant the minimum set of permissions required.
- Okta Group: SSO grouping used to enforce role-based access.
